subject: english
question:
Arrange to form a meaningful sequence:
(1) The alarm buzzed.
(2) He turned it off.
(3) He woke up immediately.
(4) He got out of bed.
solution:
The correct answer is **Option 2**.

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The sequence of events must follow a logical order of actions.
 
• **Sentence 1** ("The alarm buzzed") should be the starting point as it introduces the event that triggers the subsequent actions.
 
• **Sentence 3** ("He woke up immediately") logically follows, as waking up is the immediate reaction to the alarm buzzing.
 
• **Sentence 2** ("He turned it off") comes next, as turning off the alarm follows after waking up.
 
• **Sentence 4** ("He got out of bed") is the concluding action, which occurs after turning off the alarm.
 
• Thus, the correct sequence is: **1-3-2-4**.

 

**Coherent sequence after rearrangement**:

"The alarm buzzed. He woke up immediately. He turned it off. He got out of bed."

 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• To ensure logical flow, identify the event that initiates the sequence and follow the natural progression of actions.
 
• Focus on the cause-and-effect relationship between the sentences to determine the correct order.
